reason: Seed dispersal at the world seems the most direct way to let growth spread beyond view.
expectation: Dispersed seeds will begin spreading through the recovering world.

effect: Seed dispersal has no available combination, so I need another way to begin growth.
reaction: The direct approach did not work, which was a little surprising.
reason: Inspecting the world should reveal which available ingredient can act there.
expectation: The inspection will identify an ingredient that can start growth in the world.

effect: The world hotspot currently has no available operation, so growth must begin with the items.
reaction: That is less direct than I expected.
reason: Seeds and soil are the clearest available ingredients for starting new growth.
expectation: The seeds will germinate or establish new growth in the soil.

effect: Seeds combined with Seasons instead, revealing dormancy as the first stage of growth.
reaction: The seasonal pause is a more interesting beginning than immediate germination.
reason: Dormant seeds may now be ready to grow in soil.
expectation: The seeds will establish new growth in the soil.

effect: Dormant seeds needed dispersal first, producing scattered seeds rather than growing directly in soil.
reaction: The sequence is clearer now, though the soil guess was premature.
reason: Scattered seeds can plausibly establish themselves in soil.
expectation: Some scattered seeds will germinate in the soil.

effect: The scattered seeds established a young grove, bringing growth closer to the recovering world.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the seeds finally take root.
reason: The young grove may now be ready to grow within the world after the ice.
expectation: The grove will become part of the recovering world and continue spreading.

effect: The young grove became a forest beyond the horizon, completing the goal and showing growth and decomposition continuing without my intervention.
reaction: The open-ended ending was satisfying: the world can keep changing without another command.

mostWorthwhile.text: Placing the young grove in the world brought the seed sequence to a satisfying close, with a clear image of growth and fallen wood sustaining other lives beyond view.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the world revealed no available operation, so it did little to clarify how to start.

surprise.text: I expected seeds to grow directly in soil, but they first combined with seasons to become dormant, then needed dispersal.

arbitrary.text: The required order of dormancy and dispersal was not obvious from the initial goal, although dormancy itself had a clear explanation.

continue.text: Yes. The ending makes me curious about what the world might do without direct intervention, though the chapter's required sequence was sometimes opaque.
